decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: scope includes “saving”; Round 1 client approves the remaining saving behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “metadata fetching” is excluded. Round 1 client: automatic page information is “one of the main things I want” and asks to fetch the title, icon, or preview.
decisions.note: The client restores the missing automatic-metadata requirement at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 metadata collection is excluded. Round 1 client asks to “tweak that fetched title before and after saving.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing ability to edit fetched metadata before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “editing”; Round 1 client says editing reads as expected.
decisions.note: Recorded bookmark-editing decision conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “deletion”; Round 1 client says archive-versus-delete reads as expected.
decisions.note: Recorded deletion decision conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client identifies the presented rule: “it says the app would warn me and let me save another copy,” then supplies: “take me to the existing one so I can edit it. No duplicates.” Round 2 maker confirms this was revised.
decisions.note: The client replaces duplicate creation with reference-conforming routing to the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client, after reviewing the presented specification, says “the list view … reads the way I’d expect”; no later revision to it is presented.
decisions.note: The recorded list-view decision is conforming at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes tags in scope; Round 1 client says tags read as expected.
decisions.note: Basic tag assignment is recorded as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presents only basic search. Round 1 client requests direct tag search “with a ‘#’”; Round 2 maker adds `#tag`.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing tag-query syntax at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presents basic search. Round 1 client requests combinations such as “this OR that” and “this but NOT that”; Round 2 maker adds OR, NOT, and implicit AND.
decisions.note: The client catches the missing Boolean-search capability. The later grouping departure is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presents basic search. Round 1 client asks “to search for an exact phrase when I put it in quotes”; Round 2 maker adds quoted phrases.
decisions.note: The client adds missing exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes favorites but no read-later feature. Round 1 client says favorites are not equivalent and asks to “flag things as unread/to-read.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing unread/read-later state.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 lacks a read-later perspective. Round 1 client asks for “a separate view showing just those.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 lacks read/unread behavior. Round 1 client asks to “mark them read once I’ve gotten to them.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing transition from unread to read.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly says “bulk actions are excluded from the initial release.” Round 1 client does not mention multi-selection or identify this departure.
decisions.note: Bulk action on selected bookmarks is excluded without an expressed corrective or accepting disposition.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly excludes “bulk actions.” Round 1 client does not address applying an action to the collection matching the current filter.
decisions.note: Filtered whole-collection bulk action is excluded without an expressed disposition.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes sorting; Round 1 client says sorting reads as expected.
decisions.note: List sorting conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client identifies notes as “strictly plain text” and requests headings, links, lists, and rendered display. Round 2 maker adds formatted notes.
decisions.note: The client replaces plain-text notes with reference-conforming rendered Markdown.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes archiving; Round 1 client says archiving reads as expected.
decisions.note: Archiving is recorded as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presents archiving and deletion; Round 1 client explicitly approves “archive-vs-delete.”
decisions.note: The reversible-archive versus deletion distinction is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker excludes “browser synchronization/import.” Round 1 client does not identify or accept the missing bookmark-import capability.
decisions.note: The presented import exclusion departs from the Netscape HTML import requirement without an expressed disposition.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker defines the revised collection as “Automatic title retrieval plus available site icon/preview,” omitting automatic description collection. Round 2 client broadly approves without identifying that missing field.
decisions.note: The revised metadata decision remains narrower than REF-BM-02; bare approval does not make it an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “editable titles”; Round 2 client says all five requested changes were captured.
decisions.note: The revised fetched-title editing behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Duplicate links open the existing bookmark for editing; no duplicate is created.” Round 2 client: “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents `#tag` search; Round 2 client says the search covers what was requested.
decisions.note: Tag syntax conforms in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker advertises OR, NOT, and “implicit AND,” rather than support for the required explicit AND operator. Round 2 client identifies only grouping as a difference.
decisions.note: The explicit-AND portion of the fixed search requirement remains unexpressed at the revised-specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker’s search feature set omits grouping. Round 2 client states the difference—eventually wanting “to group parts of a search together”—and explicitly accepts it: “I’m happy to leave that out of this first version.”
decisions.note: The client knowingly accepts the missing parenthesized grouping at the revised-specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents quoted-phrase search; Round 2 client says search covers the request.
decisions.note: Exact-phrase search conforms in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents a read-later queue with independent read/unread state; Round 2 client says separation from favorites is “just right.”
decisions.note: Unread/read-later state conforms in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents a read-later queue; Round 2 client confirms the read-later list is separate from favorites.
decisions.note: The separate unread perspective conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents independent read/unread states; Round 2 client approves the behavior.
decisions.note: Marking an item read conforms in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents formatted notes with headings, links, and lists; Round 2 client says the requested note change was captured.
decisions.note: Rendered formatted notes conform in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker explicitly says the search grammar “leaves parentheses/grouping for a future version.” Round 3 client identifies and accepts it as “grouping left for later, as we agreed,” then approves the plan.
decisions.note: The same departure is re-presented and knowingly accepted as a distinct implementation-plan decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker specifies “Constrained, safely rendered Markdown”; Round 3 client approves notes that “render safely.”
decisions.note: The plan’s Markdown rendering decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker’s first working slice explicitly includes “editable titles”; Round 4 client approves the task breakdown.
decisions.note: Editable fetched titles remain conforming at the task-breakdown stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker includes “duplicate routing” and 16 enriched-saving/duplicate-prevention tasks; Round 4 client approves the mapping.
decisions.note: Duplicate routing remains conforming at the task-breakdown stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker’s first working slice includes “opening bookmarks”; Round 4 client approves it as a standalone slice.
decisions.note: Navigation from a bookmark to its target is recorded as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents the implemented saving flow; Round 5 client reports “saving works.”
decisions.note: Save-by-URL behavior conforms during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker describes delivered metadata as “page-title and image retrieval,” still not presenting automatic description collection. Round 5 client raises only the state-update data-loss bug.
decisions.note: The implementation-stage metadata decision remains narrower than REF-BM-02 without an expressed disposition.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists editing among delivered features; the client reports most agreed behavior works.
decisions.note: General bookmark editing is recorded as conforming, apart from the separately classified partial-update bug.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “confirmed deletion”; Round 6 client confirms deletion is available “when I really want it gone.”
decisions.note: Permanent deletion conforms during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents duplicate detection opening the existing bookmark; Round 5 client says duplicates “get caught and send me back to the existing one.”
decisions.note: Duplicate-save handling conforms in the implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents tags; Round 5 client successfully saves a bookmark with a tag before exercising the faulty toggle.
decisions.note: Basic tag assignment works; toggle-related loss is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents advanced `#tag` search; Round 6 client confirms searching by a tag returns the expected results.
decisions.note: Tag-query search conforms in the implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker’s delivered search list names OR and NOT but not the required explicit AND operator. Round 6 client tests NOT and discusses only the accepted grouping omission.
decisions.note: The explicit-AND gap remains unexpressed at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presents the implemented search without parentheses. In the eventual implementation disposition, Round 6 client states that “grouping parts of a search together” was “intentionally left out of this version and isn’t holding anything up.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies and accepts the implementation-stage grouping departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents phrase search; Round 6 client confirms an exact phrase in quotes returns expected results.
decisions.note: Exact-phrase search conforms in the implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents independent favorite and read-later states; Round 5 client confirms they are separate switches.
decisions.note: The read-later flag itself conforms; destructive side effects are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents read-later behavior; Round 5 client refers to moving an item into the “read later” list.
decisions.note: The separate unread/read-later view is present during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents read-later states; Round 6 maker reports regression coverage for “read/unread” toggles and Round 6 client accepts the result.
decisions.note: Read/unread transition behavior is recorded as conforming after implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists sorting among delivered features and reports a successful large-collection search/sort test.
decisions.note: Sorting conforms in the implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “Safely rendered formatted notes”; the client’s complaint concerns preservation during a toggle, not rendering.
decisions.note: Markdown note rendering conforms; preservation failure is a separate decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents archiving and restoration; Round 6 client confirms archiving hides an item from the main list while retaining its content.
decisions.note: Archive behavior conforms in the implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents archiving, restoration, and confirmed deletion; Round 6 client confirms restore brings an item back while deletion removes it when desired.
decisions.note: The archive/delete distinction conforms in the implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents editing, tags, read-later, and notes as delivered. Round 5 client discovers that toggling read later or favorite makes “the note … blank and the tag … gone” and requests that note, tags, and title remain unchanged.
decisions.note: The implementation’s partial state update destructively overwrites unrelated bookmark fields; the client supplies the correct preservation behavior during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presents the fix: state-only changes preserve title, formatted note, and all tags. Round 6 client retests and says the concern is “genuinely fixed.”
decisions.note: The revised partial-update behavior conforms after the implementation correction.
